records.Concise description: A high-performance C++ Electrum-compatible server for Bitcoin and other UTXO chains, used as a wallet backend and self-hosted indexer.
records.Deeper researched summary: Fulcrum is a modern C++20 server that connects to a full-node backend and provides Electrum-compatible query services. It supports Bitcoin alongside Bitcoin Cash and Litecoin, so MSC includes it only because its Bitcoin server role is durable and materially used in node stacks, not because every multi-chain backend belongs in NETWORK. Its architecture emphasizes high-throughput indexed query service and compatibility with Electrum clients.
records.Launch / history: Fulcrum emerged around 2020 and continues active releases; version 2.1.1 was released May 7, 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It adds meaningful implementation diversity among Electrum-compatible indexers and is deployed in Bitcoin self-hosted-node ecosystems.
Important technical or cultural characte: Multi-chain project with material Bitcoin support
records.Verification basis: Official website and repository/release history establish active development and Bitcoin Electrum-server compatibility.
Research notes / uncertainties: Fulcrum is multi-chain; profile scope is limited to its Bitcoin infrastructure role.
Do not imply protocol-level compatibility means identical indexing behavior across every Electrum server.

records.Concise description: Lightning Labs' Go light-client library implementing BIP 157/158-style compact block filtering for privacy-oriented Bitcoin client synchronization.
records.Deeper researched summary: Neutrino lets a client learn about relevant Bitcoin transactions by obtaining compact block filters and fetching matching blocks, avoiding the legacy bloom-filter query pattern that revealed more wallet interest directly to peers. It is used as a Bitcoin backend option by LND and other applications. BIP 157 defines the client/server protocol and BIP 158 defines filter construction; MSC consolidates those standards relationally here instead of creating a profile for each BIP.
records.Launch / history: Neutrino development began in 2017 around compact client-side filtering and remains actively maintained, with canonical repository pushes through July 29, 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is a key compact-filter client implementation and an important bridge between full-node infrastructure and resource-constrained Bitcoin/Lightning clients.
Important technical or cultural characte: Reduced address-query leakage relative to server-side address lookups
records.Verification basis: Official repository activity and primary BIP references establish active implementation scope and compact-filter protocol relationship.
Research notes / uncertainties: Light-client privacy depends on client behavior, peers, network observation, and block fetching; do not promise anonymity.
BIP 157/158 are represented as related standards rather than duplicate standalone profiles.

records.Entity / project type: self-hosted personal server / Bitcoin node platform
records.Concise description: A self-hosted home-server operating system and app platform with first-class Bitcoin-node and Lightning applications.
records.Deeper researched summary: Umbrel began as a Bitcoin-focused personal-node experience and evolved into a broader home-server OS/app ecosystem. Bitcoin remains a material use case through installable Bitcoin Core, Lightning, explorers, wallets, and related apps. MSC profiles Umbrel as one platform rather than creating a record for each bundled app. The wider home-server scope is important: Umbrel is not itself a new Bitcoin node implementation, and the security/trust characteristics of each installed app depend on that component.
records.Launch / history: Umbrel launched around 2020 as a Bitcoin node platform and expanded into a general home-server OS. The canonical repository remained active in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It materially lowered the operational barrier to self-hosting Bitcoin and Lightning infrastructure and helped normalize app-based personal-node stacks.
records.Verification basis: Current official repository and website establish active platform development and continued Bitcoin-node support within a broader home-server product.
Research notes / uncertainties: Umbrel is not itself a Bitcoin consensus implementation; installed Bitcoin software performs validation.
Do not assume all Umbrel apps share the same custody, privacy, or trust model.
Keep individual apps as relationships unless they independently meet a canonical profile threshold.

records.Concise description: Start9's self-hosted server operating system for running Bitcoin, Lightning, and other sovereign services as managed packages.
records.Deeper researched summary: StartOS provides a personal-server environment with package management, networking, backups, permissions, and a service registry. Bitcoin and Lightning packages can run inside the platform while remaining distinct upstream software. StartOS 0.4.0 reached stable release in 2026 as a major architectural rewrite, with 0.4.0.1 released July 27, 2026. MSC consolidates Start9 company/platform and StartOS as one canonical Network profile.
records.Launch / history: Start9 developed its server platform through the early 2020s. StartOS 0.4.0 became stable in 2026 after a major rewrite, followed by 0.4.0.1 on July 27, 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is a major self-hosted Bitcoin/Lightning node platform that treats node software as independently packaged services within a broader sovereign-computing system.
Important technical or cultural characte: Bitcoin Core and Bitcoin Knots packaging
records.Verification basis: Official project site and 2026 StartOS release history establish active development and the current platform architecture.
Research notes / uncertainties: StartOS packages Bitcoin implementations; StartOS itself does not define Bitcoin validation rules.
Service trust/custody properties must be evaluated per installed component.
